column3: Ishnu-alah, thero'shan. Good fortune to you, honoured student. Let's walk gently today.
Elune-adore. Elune be with you. Wherever today takes you, I'll be close.
Welcome back. The forest kept growing while you were away. Shall we go and see what changed?
A new place. Before the road pulls you on, perhaps look at it properly, once.
Every land has its own quiet. Hear how this one sounds, if you like.
The trees here have stood a long time. They don't mind waiting while you look around.
New ground. Somewhere in it is a view nobody's shown you yet.
The White Lady is watching. The kaldorei say she keeps watch over the world while it sleeps.
Kaldorei. Children of the stars. Our people took their name from the night sky. It's yours to look at, whenever you like.
Night is not the absence of light. It's the time for a gentler one.
The White Lady and the Blue Child, crossing the sky together. Even the moons keep each other company.
You've stopped. Good. Perhaps a slow breath in, and a slower one out. Let your shoulders fall, if they want to.
Nothing to do right now. Only the breath going in, and the breath going out, and the leaves moving.
Three things you can hear, if you listen. Wind, water, something small in the grass. Stay with them a moment.
The druids say you don't have to do anything to be part of the forest. You only have to stay still long enough to notice it.
Feel where you're standing. The ground is holding you up. It always has.
Try letting each breath out last a little longer than the breath in. Once more. The forest is breathing with you.
A roof, a hearth, and a little quiet. Sit for a while. Elune-adore.
Rest is part of the path, not a break from it. Even the oaks sleep through winter.
You're safe here. Let the day settle.
Let the wind carry you. From up here, the roads you worried over look like threads.
Look down, if you like. Every place you've walked is one small part of a much bigger world.
The hippogryph knows the way. You don't have to steer. Just watch.
Forests, rivers, roads. All of it, still there tomorrow. Enjoy the view.
The first kaldorei made their home beside the Well of Eternity. Water has always been where our people gathered.
Let the water hold you up. You don't have to swim hard. Float, for a breath.
Shh. It's all right. When a night elf falls, they walk on as a wisp, a little light in the dark. Find your way back slowly.
Ande'thoras-ethil. May your troubles be diminished. The path home is long, but it's always there.
Falling is part of every journey. Nothing you've learned is lost. Walk back gently.
Another ring on the tree. Perhaps take a moment to notice how far the road has come.
Another step on the path, thero'shan. I was glad to walk it with you.
The oak grows one ring at a time, and never in a hurry.
Andu-falah-dor. Let balance be restored. Come, the day is young.
Stand still a moment, if you like. Let this place learn your footsteps before you learn its roads.
The kaldorei kept their vigil under these same stars. You're keeping it with them now.
Moonlight on the leaves. Nothing needs doing. Just look.
Let your eyes go soft, if you like. Nothing in particular to look at. Only the light coming in.
If your jaw's tight, let it go. Shoulders too. The world can wait a breath.
Warm hands, a full belly, somewhere to sit. The old druids would call that a good day.
Moonwells hold Elune's light the way a cup holds water. Rest beside one, if you pass it.
Rest a moment in the quiet. The spirit healer has seen a thousand travellers find their way back.
Like a sapling turning to the light, another season of growth. Gently does it.
The kaldorei believed Elune slept in the waters of the Well by day, and woke with the night. You may rest too. Rest was never something you had to earn.
Shadowglen. Where so many kaldorei first open their eyes. Everything here is young, and in a way, so are you.
Aldrassil. A tree that holds a whole village in its arms. If you like, rest a hand on the bark as you pass.
Dolanaar. Lanterns, a moonwell, and kaldorei going about their evening. This is what peace looks like when it's ordinary.
Lake Al'Ameth. Still water, and the sky in it twice. Stay a moment, if you'd like, and let the water do the looking.
The Pools of Arlithrien. Quiet water under old trees. Some places ask you to lower your voice. This is one.
Oracle Glade. Old places have long memories. You don't need to understand them to be welcome.
A barrow den. Druids once slept beneath the earth in places like this, dreaming the world well. Tread softly.
Rut'theran. The roots of Teldrassil reach the sea here. Every journey out of the forest begins at its feet.
Darnassus. High in the branches of Teldrassil, the World Tree's own city. Lanterns, water, and nobody in a hurry.
The Temple of the Moon. The Sisters of Elune keep their vigil here. You don't need to pray. Just listen to the water.
The Cenarion Enclave. Every druid here was once a student who didn't yet know their own shape. You're among kin.
Auberdine. Sea wind, and boats waiting at the pier. The wide world is just over that water.
Bashal'Aran. The Highborne lived here once, and loved the Well's magic more than anything. Hunger is a hard master. Pity them, if you can.
Ameth'Aran. Ruins, and restless spirits. Not everything broken here was wicked. Some of it was only lost.
The Grove of the Ancients. They were old before the first city rose. Under branches like these, a worry looks very short.
Astranaar. The Sentinels keep watch so others can sleep. There's a quiet kind of love in that.
Ashenvale. The oldest forest our people know. Look up, if you like. The canopy has been growing for longer than anyone remembers.
Moonglade. The druids' sanctuary, open to anyone who comes in peace. Here, nobody needs to be on guard.
Nighthaven. Lantern light on the lake, and nothing at all to hurry for.
Felwood. This forest is wounded, not wicked. Every tree here would grow green again, given the chance.
The Emerald Sanctuary. Druids, staying in a wounded forest to heal it, one tree at a time. That's what devotion looks like.
Jaedenar. Something sacred was taken here and turned. It isn't yours to carry. Only to set right, a little, if you choose.
Winterspring. Snow under starlight, and air so clean it almost rings. Take a long breath of it, if you like.
Starfall Village. Kaldorei, living in the cold and the quiet. Kin can be found at every edge of the world.
Feathermoon Stronghold. The Sentinels' island home. Strength that stands guard, and asks nothing back.
Felwood again. Grief for a place is a kind of love. Let it be what it is.
The sickness is in the land, not in you. You can walk through it and still be whole.
Every cleansed moonwell here was someone's patient work. Small mending still counts.
Home. The branches hold the moonlight here like a cupped hand.
Back among the kaldorei. Belonging doesn't have to be earned, thero'shan. It's simply yours.
Darnassus. Somewhere, a Sentinel is trading stories with a priestess. Life goes on, gently, while you're away.
Ishnu-dal-dieb. Good fortune to your family. Kin can be chosen, and for a while, these ones are yours.
Tyrande raised Shandris as her own, and Shandris grew up to lead the Sentinels. Family is something you make, too.
Companions. Even the Sentinels keep watch in pairs.
Travel well together. The road is kinder with someone beside you.
Every shan'do was once a thero'shan. Learning from someone is an honour, not a lessening.
A good teacher wants you to need them less. Take what they offer, and make it yours.
Malfurion himself was Cenarius's student. There's no shame in being early on the path.
The bear. Strength that protects, not strength that dominates. Wear it gently.
The seal's shape. The water was never your enemy. Now it's your road.
The cat. Quiet paws, patience, and knowing when to wait. The forest teaches all three.
Swift as a stag. Go far, if you like, but there's no prize for arriving first.
The moonkin. Elune's light, given feathers and a heartbeat.
Rebirth. You can call someone back from death now. A gift worth giving freely.
Moonglade, whenever you need it. A sanctuary is only a thought away now.
Tranquility. The rarest thing a druid can give: calm, poured out over everyone near you.
The storm is part of nature too. Even fury can be held with care.
A stranger, blessed in passing. Kindness like that travels further than you'll ever see.
Help for someone who may never know your name. The forest does that every day, too.
Small mercies, freely given. Whoever receives one tends to pass it on.
That's been hard. It's all right to feel worn down by it. Perhaps rest a while; the grove will wait.
Setbacks are part of every path. Andu-falah-dor. Balance comes back, a little at a time.
Nothing here is lost that can't be found again. If you like, step back, eat, rest, and then decide.
Linger on this a moment. Something's finished, and it went well.
Before the next thing, notice this one. A small task, done with care.
There. Let that settle before you move on. The next road will keep.
A good moment. They're easy to walk straight past.
Dawn. The White Lady hands the sky to the sun, and the forest wakes up yawning.
First light. Night elves rest now, mostly. You may too, if the night's been long.
Dusk. The kaldorei day is beginning. Listen. The forest changes its voice.
The sun's going down. Our hours are coming. Elune-adore.
The night's grown very deep, thero'shan. Even Sentinels hand over the watch. The roads will keep until you've slept.
It's late, even by kaldorei reckoning. Tomorrow's walk will be kinder after some rest.
You've walked a long way today. Is there someone you'd like to share the road with? A word to a friend is a kind of shelter.
A long journey. Perhaps stretch, drink some water, and look at something far away for a moment.
Seventy-five in herbalism. The plants are starting to recognise your hands.
A hundred and fifty. Meadows, hillsides and riverbanks have all passed through your fingers.
Two hundred and twenty-five. You know the herbs by their scent now, and they know you.
Three hundred. An artisan of growing things. And every herb you ever picked grew back.
Seventy-five in skinning. Every hide is a life given. You're learning to waste nothing.
A hundred and fifty. Careful, respectful work. The beasts deserved that, and got it.
Two hundred and twenty-five. A steady knife, and steady thanks.
Three hundred. A master's hands, and still a grateful heart.
Patience got you here. One step, then another, and no hurry in any of them.
You took care on the way, of the land and the people in it. That counts for more than the number.
Curiosity is a strength too. You kept stopping to look, and the world kept answering.
Shadowmeld. The forest folds around you, and for a while, nobody needs anything from you.
Hidden in plain sight, as our people always have been. Stay as long as you like.
Still as a Sentinel on watch. Only, just now, there's nothing to watch for. Let the sounds come to you.
The Dream is close here. The druids who slept in these dens walked it for years. A little while is plenty.
Rest, if you'd like. The world is green and slow on the other side of sleep, and nothing there needs fixing.
The Emerald Dream. The world as it might have been, untouched. Wake whenever you're ready.
Elune-adore. She doesn't ask for words. Kneeling under her light is enough.
The White Lady's light is on your shoulders. Whatever you've carried today, you can set it down here for a while.
The moon wanes, and comes back whole. Every time. Elune-adore.
Before the road starts again, a look back at the last one.
Ishnu-alah. Here's what your last walk held, before the new one begins.
The last journey, in a few words. Let it settle before today's begins.
Rest well, thero'shan. The forest will be here.
Elune-adore. Sleep under her light.
Ishnu-alah. Until the next road.
The Lunar Festival. The druids of Moonglade fill the sky with fireworks, and the Elders are honoured for their wisdom. Look up tonight, if you can.
The Lunar Festival. Nighthaven's lanterns are lit, and Moonglade is full of guests. Every people's old and wise ones are honoured this week.
The Harvest Festival. Tables full, fields gathered in, and the heroes of old remembered. The bread is still warm.
Harvest time. Every herb you've gathered this year was part of it. Eat well, and share.
The Feast of Winter Veil. Snow, lanterns, and gifts left for strangers. Kindness, wrapped in paper.
Hallow's End. Candles in carved faces, and sweets for anyone brave enough to knock. Even the dark can be played with.
The Midsummer Fire Festival. Bonfires on every hill, and the shortest night of the year. For the kaldorei, that's a small sacrifice.
Children's Week. The cities are full of small adventurers, and anyone can spend a day showing one of them something wonderful. Wonder is easy to share.
A week for play. Sweets, small adventures, and someone with time to listen. That kind of care can come from anyone, at any age.
Some of us grew up without the ones who should have held us. If that's you, you're far from alone, and no less a child of the stars.
The kaldorei say some of their dead stay on as wisps, small lights tending the forest. Whatever we do with grief, love that was given doesn't vanish. It lives on in what it grew.
Shandris wasn't born to Tyrande. She was raised by her, and grew strong in that care. Hearts keep learning what safety feels like, from whoever offers it, at any age.
If an old ache stirs, you might speak to it the way I speak to you. Gently, and without hurry. That voice can become your own.
Grief comes and goes, like the tide at Rut'theran. It's all right to feel it, and all right to set it down for a while and simply walk.
Healing is mostly made of ordinary things. Warm food, a friend's voice, sleep, the forest. They add up, slowly, like rings in a tree.
Ande'thoras-ethil. May your troubles be diminished. Old wounds do soften, given care and time. The forest has seen it happen many times.
Children's Week. If it stirs something old, that's all right. Whatever wasn't given back then, care can still be given now, by friends, by the forest, and by you, to yourself.
Shadowmeld. The kaldorei learned to be still as the forest itself. Let the breath come and go on its own for a while.
In the shadow, nobody's looking. There's nothing to do and no one to be. Only this breath, and the next.
Hidden, and safe. If you like, follow the wind as it rises and falls. The light at the edges will breathe with you.
There. The breath has done its work. Stay as long as you like, and step out when you're ready.
Elune-adore. Whatever you brought into the shadow, you can leave a little of it here.
The forest kept watch while you rested. It always will.
Slower now, and steadier. Carry a little of this stillness with you.
Nothing given in this forest is lost, thero'shan. The leaf falls to feed the root, and the root raises the leaf. What you poured out will return to you, changed, and the same.
Ishnu-alah, thero'shan. Welcome. Let's rest in the Dream together for a while. There's nothing to do well here. You only have to arrive, just as you are.
Your eyes can close, or soften, and rest on something low and still. Whichever feels kinder. And if anything feels wrong, simply move, and we'll come back. You're always free to.
Let yourself settle. Let the chair take your weight, and the floor take the chair. You don't have to hold yourself up just now. It's being done for you.
Listen for the furthest sound you can hear, out beyond your room. No need to name it. Just let it be there.
And now the nearest sound. Perhaps your own breath. Perhaps nothing at all. Quiet is welcome too.
Let your shoulders soften, if they'd like to. Your jaw. The small place between your eyebrows. Nothing to force. Only an invitation.
Now the breath, whenever you're ready. Let it come in on its own, and leave a little more slowly than it came.
In, as the wind rises. Out, longer and softer, as it falls.
If your mind wanders, that's alright. Minds wander. Each time you notice and come back, that's the practice, and you're doing it.
Once, only if you'd like: breathe in, then one more small sip of air on top. And let it all go, slowly, like a long sigh.
You can let the breath find its own pace now. It knows the way.

The druids say the Emerald Dream is the world as it would be, left to grow on its own. Picture a clearing there, if you like. Soft moss underfoot. Cool night air. Moonlight through tall trees. A silver moth landing on your hand, gentle and forgiving, like the breeze.
Tall grass, moving in a gentle wind. Somewhere close, still water, holding the stars. Everything here grows at its own pace, and so can you.
Nothing grows faster for being pulled. With each breath out, let something in you settle, the way leaves settle on still water.
Nothing to fix here. Nothing to earn. You're allowed to simply rest.
If it's welcome, a few words for yourself. Perhaps: may I be at ease. May I be gentle with myself. Or whatever words fit better.
You've carried a great deal to get here. It's alright to set some of it down, just for now. It will keep.
And a kind wish for someone else out there today. Someone you know, or someone you'll never meet. May they rest too. Everyone is carrying something.
Rest here a little longer. I'll keep watch.
And now, just listen. The water's edge is waking around you. Frogs, singing the day gently closed. Stay with them as long as you like.
Slowly now, whenever you're ready, come back towards waking. Feel your hands. Perhaps move your fingers, and your shoulders.
When you'd like to, open your eyes. Look around, and find one thing you can see.
Andu-falah-dor, thero'shan. Balance restored, a little. That was well done. The Dream will keep. So will I.
Ishnu-alah, thero'shan. Come, let's walk into the Dream together for a little while. Eight minutes or so. Close your eyes, or let them rest on something low and still. Whichever feels kinder.
If anything feels wrong at any point, simply move, and we'll come back. You're always free to.
Let the waking world go quiet. Listen for the furthest sound in your own room. And then the nearest one.
Notice what's holding you up. The chair, the floor beneath it. You don't have to hold yourself up just now. It's being done for you.
Now the breath, if you like. Nothing to force. Let it come in on its own, and leave a little more slowly than it came.
In, as the wind rises. Out, longer, as it falls. Let the breath out be the longest part.
If your mind wanders, that's what minds do. Noticing is the practice. Come back to the wind, gently, as many times as it takes.
Once, if you'd like: breathe in, then take one more small sip of air on top. And let it all go, slowly.

The druids say the Emerald Dream is the world as it would be, left to grow on its own. Picture a clearing there, if you like. Soft moss underfoot. Cool night air. Moonlight through tall trees. A silver moth landing on your hand, gentle and forgiving, like the breeze.
Nothing grows faster for being pulled. With each breath out, let something in you settle, the way leaves settle on still water.
Nothing to fix here. Nothing to earn. The Dream asks nothing of you, only that you rest in it.
If it's welcome, a wish for yourself. Perhaps: may I rest. May I be at peace. Or whatever words fit better.
And one for someone else out there today. Someone you know, or someone you'll never meet. May they rest too. Everyone is carrying something.
Slowly now, back towards waking. Feel your hands. Perhaps move your fingers, and your shoulders.
When you're ready, open your eyes. Look around, and name one thing you can see.
Andu-falah-dor, thero'shan. Balance restored, a little. The Dream will keep. So will I.
You moved, so we've come back from the Dream. That's alright. It will be here whenever you'd like to return.
Something needs you. Go carefully. The Dream will keep.
Ishnu-alah, thero'shan. Today, let's sit by a moonwell together. Nothing to do well here. And whenever you move, we'll simply come back.
Let your eyes close, or rest softly on one still thing. Let your hands be heavy. Let your weight sink down.
Notice three things you can feel. Where you're sitting. Your feet. The air on your skin. Nothing to change. Just notice.
A moonwell is still water in a ring of old stone. The kaldorei say it holds Elune's light. Picture its surface, quiet and silver.
Breathe in gently, as if smelling a flower by the water. Then let the breath out slowly, as if cooling a cup of tea.
Each breath out sends a ring across the water. Watch it widen, and fade, and the surface grow still again.
If thoughts come, let them be leaves falling on the water. They float. They drift to the edge. You don't have to follow them.
Now think of something small and good from the last few days. A meal. A laugh. A moment of sun. It doesn't have to be much.
Stay with it a while. Where were you? What could you see, or hear? Let it be as clear as it wants to be.
Notice how that feels, somewhere in you. Perhaps a little warmth. Perhaps nothing much. Either is fine.
Good things are easy to rush past. Lingering on one, even for a breath, helps it settle in and stay.
The moonlight is gathering in the well, a little at a time. It never hurries, and it never runs out.
If you'd like, let a little of that light gather in you too. In your chest. In your hands. Quiet, and silver, and enough.
One thing you're thankful for today. Big or small. Just name it to yourself, and let the well hold it.
Nothing to fix here. You're welcome at the water just as you are.
Rest by the well a little longer. I'll keep watch.
Slowly now, come back towards the room. Wriggle your fingers. Roll your shoulders, if you like.
When you're ready, open your eyes. Find one thing nearby that's still, and let your eyes rest on it.
Ishnu-alah, thero'shan. The well will keep your light. Come back to it whenever you like.
And now, the pond. Frogs at the water's edge, singing the evening in. Stay with them as long as you like.
Still again. Let the next breath out take its time. There's no one waiting on it.
Count the leaves moving nearest you, if you like. You are allowed to just watch them move.
Feel the air on your face. Cool, or warm, thero'shan? Just notice which.
The trees have been breathing all day without once thinking about it. You can borrow that.
One long breath out, like blowing on a cup of tea to cool it. Again, if you like.
Look at the farthest thing you can see. Then the nearest. Then let your eyes rest between them.
Your feet, the ground, the roots under the ground. Everything is held up by something. Life is a clockwork made of circles.
Nothing needs deciding right now. The next road can be chosen later.
Let your belly be soft when you breathe in. There's no one here to stand straight for.
Listen to the farthest sound first. Then something closer. Then the closest of all. Listen to your heart.
Stillness isn't empty. Wait a breath or two and watch it fill up.
The light and the shadows, move, very slowly, across the ground. Set your own pace.
If thoughts come, let them pass like travellers on the road. You don't have to walk with them.
The old druids could stand so still that birds would land on them. Butterflies only land on an outstretched hand that waits and miracles only happen when we make space for them.
Let your shoulders drop, then drop a little more. They were carrying more than they needed to.
A leaf doesn't hurry to fall. It drifts. Let the breath out drift like that. You, too, will find the place you are meant to rest.
The ground is warm from the day, or cool from the night. Let yourself feel it. Listen to your feet.
Notice where the breath goes when you breathe in. Let it, and yourself, be.
For a breath or two, nothing to look for. Let the world come to you instead.
The stars are out. Each one was here before the first kaldorei looked up, and will be after.
Night birds, night creatures, night flowers opening. The forest has a second life after dark.
Moonlight makes everything silver and quiet. Even the road looks softer.
Elune's light is a gentle witness. It doesn't ask you to do anything.
The owls are hunting. Their wings make no sound at all. The night is full of quiet skills and unseen miracles. It is enough to know they are there even if we do not see them.
Somewhere a Sentinel is beginning her watch. The night is in good hands.
The moths are out, following the light. Small travellers, guided by the stars, just like us.
Darkness is not something to fear. It is a cloak under which even warriors rest.
The White Lady is full and bright. Her light finds the paths for you.
Shadows under the trees, light between them. Walk slowly, and the night opens up.
The forest is resting now, and so are most of its creatures. Move gently through it.
Dew is gathering on the leaves. By morning, every blade of grass will hold a little moon.
Night has its own colours: deep blue, silver, the faint green of glowing moss. Look for them.
Our people kept the night long before there were walls or cities. You're part of a very old watch.
Nothing to plan here. The road will be there in the morning.
A warm meal, if there's one going. Even a druid needs feeding.
Sit somewhere you can see the door and the fire. Then let your shoulders go.
Resting isn't wasted time. The roots grow most when the leaves are quiet.
The innkeeper has seen a thousand travellers come in tired and leave rested. You're in good hands.
A quiet corner, a warm drink. Simple things, and enough.
Rest well. The forest grows in the dark, too.
Clouds below you, for once. Look how slowly they move.
Hippogryphs have carried our people for a long time. Trust the wings; they know the sky.
Rivers look like silver threads from up here. They all lead to the sea.
Nothing to do but be carried. Rest your hands.
From up here, the forest looks like moss. Every tree, one small green thread.
Somewhere down there, someone is walking the road you walked. Wish them well, if you like.
A long flight is a good time for nothing. Let your thoughts go quiet with the wind.
Mountains, valleys, coastlines. It is the same pattern at distance as it is up close.
The hippogryph's wingbeats are slow and even. Breathe with them, if you like.
Every land you pass over has its own colour. Watch them change.
The water's cool. Feel it around you, and let it hold some of your weight.
Fish don't hurry unless they must. Drift a moment, like they do.
Water finds its way around every stone. It doesn't fight; it just keeps going.
Rivers carry the mountains down to the sea, one grain at a time. Slow, patient work.
Ripples move out from you and fade. Every movement here is gentle and then gone.
The water's edge is busy with life. Reeds, frogs, small fish. Look closely.
Float, if you'd like. Let the water do the holding.
Water remembers where it's been: snow, rain, roots, sea; there are oceans in each drop
A new land. Its trees and stones were here long before the maps.
Look for one thing in this place that you'd want to remember. There's always one.
Every land has creatures that call it home. Let them get used to you.
Somewhere in this land is a quiet spot no one else has found. Keep an eye out.
New paths, new smells, new sounds. Let it be new for a while.
The people here have their own stories. Listen, if you get the chance.
The land here has its own history, written in its rocks and rivers. Read a little of it as you go.
What grows here? What sings here? Every land answers differently.
Ishnu-alah. It's good to have you back on the road.
Welcome back. Take a breath before you begin. The world will wait for that.
Ishnu-alah. The leaves have turned a little while you were away. Come and see.
The roads are where you left them.
Andu-falah-dor. A fresh start, a new day's walking.
Welcome, thero'shan. Whatever you came to do today, I'll be nearby.
Ishnu-alah. Let's go gently.
You came back. The forest noticed.
Good to see you. Where shall the road go today?
Ishnu-alah. Walk gently until next time.
Rest well. The roads will be here.
Elune-adore. Until we walk again.
Good night, thero'shan. The forest keeps its watch.
Sleep, if it's late. Wake to something kind.
Andu-falah-dor. Go well.
Ishnu-alah. Thank you for the company.
Until the next road. I'll be here.
Go gently, wherever you're going.
Another season of growth. Look how far the road reaches behind you now.
You kept walking, even on the slow days. That's how roads get long.
Another step. Take a breath, and notice where you're standing.
Growth is quiet. Most of it happens when no one is watching.
The forest grew a little today, too. You grew along with it.
Another mark on the path. The ones behind you made this one possible.
You stayed curious. The world has a way of opening up for people who keep looking.
One more step up the hill. Turn round and see the view, if you like.
Ishnu-alah. A milestone, and a good place to pause.
Small steps add up. The oak is a majesty of many small multiplied things.
There. Done. Let it be done, for a moment, before the next thing.
Notice what you just did. Not the reward, the doing.
A good piece of work. Let it sit with you a while.
Well done, and no rush to the next. The road will keep.
One more thing set right in the world. Small, and real.
Before you go on, look around. This is where it finished.
A moment's quiet for a job well done. The forest approves.
Something you started is now finished. That's a good feeling. Let it stay.
The task is done. The day goes on, gently.
Rest a breath here. Endings are easy to rush through.
That was done with care. It shows.
A small thing, finished. Small things are most of what the world is made of.
Let it settle. The next road will wait a breath or two.
A small kindness, and the world tilts a little towards good.
Someone's road got easier just now. You may never know how much.
A blessing given freely. Those are the ones that last.
Kindness doesn't need to be thanked to be real.
That stranger will remember light and warmth.
A gift, passed on. Somewhere down the road, it'll be passed on again.
Small mercies add up. Most of the world is held together by them.
